name: Selenor Aetheis

poster.hook: By Chancery order: the Cooling Concord lapses at midnight. Attendance compulsory.
poster.reward: 25 gp a day, and the Registrar's good opinion

story.appearance: Slender, silver-haired high elf in a Chancery advocate's pale grey coat with ink-stained cuffs. A thin bronze seal-ring on every second finger, and a lute strapped across his back that he claims is for work.
story.concept: Selenor is a junior advocate of the New Ouransgard Chancery, the grandson of Aetheion the Drafter, who wrote the Cooling Concord. He negotiates the city's contracts, softens its tax disputes, and has a talent for saying the unsayable beautifully. He is good at his job and has just started to dislike what that means.
story.stake: The Chancery's budget, the city's baths and his own career all depend on renewal. His grandfather's name is on the clause that keeps Torvak in the fire.
story.goal: Renew the Concord legally, with no one hurt, and then go home and sleep for a week.
story.secret: He carries the Registrar's sealed Writ of Assumed Consent: if Torvak will not agree to renewal, Selenor is to forge the Surety's mark. He has also noticed that one page of the Chancery's copy, certified in the notaries' hall at Amberhall, is missing from the register. He told no one. He has decided nothing yet.
story.voice: Warm, measured, a touch elegiac, as if every sentence were being engraved. Never interrupts. Goes very quiet when he is angry and begins to quote statute.
mannerisms: Turns his seal-rings with his thumb while he thinks
Describes every room as if drafting its inventory
Hums a Ouran lament under his breath when nervous
story.trinket: Aetheion's pen, with a nib worn to a slant by eighty years of the wrong hand

ties.text: A decade of formal letters between the Chancery and the Driftwood tide-court. They have never met, and Selenor suspects the man writes better than he speaks.
ties.public: Ten years of formal letters; they have never met

ties.text: His grandfather drafted the clause that bound hers. He has read every word of her family's file and has not yet said so.
ties.public: His grandfather drafted the clause that bound hers

ties.text: The stoker signs the Chancery's maintenance orders in soot-black thumbprints. He has been trying to get her to use a pen for three years.
ties.public: She signs Chancery maintenance orders with a thumbprint

story.intro: "Selenor Aetheis, Chancery advocate. I'm here to see that nothing irreversible happens before breakfast."

features.name: Fey Ancestry
features.text: Advantage on saves to avoid or end the Charmed condition.

features.name: Trance
features.text: A Long Rest takes 4 hours of meditation, not sleep.

features.name: Elven Lineage (High Elf)
features.text: Know Prestidigitation. Cast Detect Magic once per Long Rest without a slot. Spell ability is Charisma.

features.name: Skilled
features.text: Proficiency in three extra skills or tools; Perception, Stealth and Calligrapher's Supplies.

features.name: Bardic Inspiration (d6)
features.text: Bonus Action: give a creature within 60 ft a d6. Within the next hour, after it fails a D20 Test, it can add the die.

features.name: Jack of All Trades
features.text: Add half your proficiency bonus to checks you are not proficient in.

features.name: Expertise
features.text: Double proficiency in Persuasion and Deception.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies (Lore)
features.text: Three more skill proficiencies: Investigation, Arcana, Religion.

features.name: Cutting Words
features.text: Reaction: spend a Bardic Inspiration die to subtract it from a creature's attack roll, damage roll or ability check within 60 ft.

attacks.name: Vicious Mockery
attacks.note: Target has disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of your next turn if it fails

spellcasting.note: Prepares 7 bard spells after a Long Rest. Spell save DC 14, spell attack +6.

flashback: What did your grandfather Aetheion say about the Concord when you were small, and what did you take him to mean?

ifUnclaimed.npc: The Chancery sends Steward Naeris Oulane to cast its vote and carry the Chancery copy. She is friendly and visibly reluctant, and she can be talked around. She cites the Chancery's line and folds when the original text is read aloud.

reassign.beat: The missing page from the Chancery copy (letter: the-drafters-seal)
reassign.text: You have noticed that the Chancery's certified copy skips a page between the fourth and fifth articles. The register says nothing. You know exactly which clause would be on it.

reassign.beat: The Registrar's Writ of Assumed Consent
reassign.text: Steward Naeris pressed a sealed Writ into your hand: if the Surety will not consent to renewal, the bearer is to mark for him. You have not broken the seal. You have not decided anything.
